items.title: [ArchDaily] Legombang Treehouse / Cave Urban
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Legombang Treehouse reinterprets traditional Balinese architecture as a contemporary tropical family home, using reclaimed timber, passive design, and a treehouse-like structure woven around the site's existing trees. Designed by Cave Urban co-founder Jed Long for his own family, the house is located in Pantai Lembeng, Ketewel, Bali. As both architect and client, Jed had the opportunity to explore his own approach to tropical family living without the constraints of a conventional client brief.

items.title: [ArchDaily] La Joya / Veö estudio
items.content_html:
On a plot of land that rises thirteen meters (forty-three feet) from the street, "La Joya" House transforms the challenge of a steep slope into an architectural journey, revealing the landscape of San Agustinillo level by level.
The project emerged from a brief to develop three independent units: two small apartments intended primarily as rentals, and a larger residence for the owners' temporary stays. Instead of concentrating the program into a conventional volume, the steep topography offered an opportunity to fragment it and distribute it across different levels along the hillside. Consequently, each unit finds its own place within the site, maintaining privacy while enjoying a direct relationship with the sea.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Herdade da Matinha Country House / Sabrab
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Between the cork oaks and the Vicentina Coast, Herdade da Matinha was born from an abandoned Alentejo estate, whose chimney still bears the date 1917. This rural tourism project, developed by SABRAB Architecture in collaboration with the owner Alfredo Moreira da Silva, starts from a simple principle: to make use of what already existed and add only what was necessary, with the same economy of means that has always characterized rural construction in the Alentejo region.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil
items.content_html: The concept of "eyes on the street" is perhaps the most famous within architectural and urban literature when it comes to urban security. Jane Jacobs uses this expression to refer to people who - consciously or unconsciously - use public spaces or observe them from their homes, generating natural surveillance. A movement that, within our discipline, is encouraged both through quality public spaces and through the powerful relationship between the public and private created through building facades. Advocating for this daily control, Jacobs believes in a way of making architecture and cities that condemns excessive verticalization, reinforced by isolated buildings and single-use ones that deny contact with the street.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Lele Hotel / The Lab Evn
items.content_html: Located in Vayots Dzor, Lele Hotel is conceived as a direct response to the character and topography of its mountainous surroundings. Rather than imposing a separate architectural object on the landscape, the design seeks continuity with the terrain through its materiality, proportions, and relationship to the existing slope.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Buenos Aires Architecture City Guide: 31 Sites Between Heritage and the Contemporary
items.content_html: Buenos Aires is a city of rich history and distinct atmospheres. There are many reasons to explore its architecture: the city is the result of a complex interplay of cultural factors shaped by a multitude of architectural styles and trends. Its streets and heterogeneous buildings define its inhabitants, reflecting an identity forged by its history.

items.title: [ArchDaily] CHYBÍK + KRIŠTOF Turns Aedes Into a Live Architecture Studio to Develop Four Berlin Projects
items.content_html: CHYBÍK + KRIŠTOF has opened Building the Existing City, an exhibition at Aedes Architecture Forum in Berlin that transforms the gallery into a working architecture studio. Running from October 23 to December 3, 2026, the exhibition centres on four architectural and urban design proposals for sites or urban situations in Berlin, selected through an open call. Over six weeks, visitors can follow the practice's research, discussions, and design work as the proposals develop, gaining insight into the processes through which architectural interventions are conceived in response to local conditions.

items.title: Pavilions as Stances: 6 Unbuilt Proposals from the ArchDaily Community
items.content_html: In architecture, the word "pavilion" can describe an endless variety of structures. It might be defined as a principle and a typology, a freestanding structure, a temporary intervention, a gathering place in the city, or a space for experimentation. This last quality is what unites the six unbuilt projects featured here, all designed and submitted by ArchDaily readers. Here, the definition lies in their sculptural qualities and formal exploration, while their permanence and location vary according to each structure's purpose. The proposals also demonstrate another quality inherent to the pavilion: the intention to symbolically represent a stance. Their exploration of form and material thus also reflects a search for a sense of boundary, wonder, or a shared future.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Dam House / 24 7 Arquitetura
items.content_html: Set on an approximately 24.000 m² site with an elevation difference of over 60 meters descending toward the reservoir, the residence emerges from a desire to establish continuity between architecture, topography and landscape. Organized across three stepped terraces, the house follows the natural contours of the land, breaking into volumes that adapt to the slope, minimize earthworks and preserve the relationship with the surrounding environment.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Parkside Villa / Studio B Architecture + Interiors
items.content_html: Situated in a rural Boulder neighborhood, Parkside Villa is a comprehensive transformation of an existing 9,100-square-foot residence, reimagined for the evolving lifestyle of an active family. Rather than demolishing and rebuilding, Studio B Architecture + Interiors approached the project as an opportunity to redefine the relationship between architecture, interiors and landscape while preserving the home's existing foundation and much of its structural framing.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Aalok Farmhouse / Nodecraft Studio
items.content_html: Aalok Farmhouse is a 3-bedroom weekend home located on the outskirts of Bengaluru that reinterprets the farmhouse typology through a series of independent pavilions connected by landscape. Rather than treating the outdoors as an extension of the built form, the project allows courtyards, trees and open thresholds to define the architecture. Designed as a retreat for family use and occasional business gatherings, the residence required a balance between privacy and collective interaction. This led the design to move away from the conventional farmhouse model of enclosed rooms connected through internal corridors. Instead, circulation is externalized, transforming movement into a sequence of shaded pathways, courtyards and framed views.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Restoring Views at Neutra’s Corwin House with Sky-Frame
items.content_html: About an hour's drive from New York, the Corwin House sits in hilly woodland high above the Saugatuck River. Completed by Richard Neutra in 1956, it is one of only three houses the architect built in Connecticut. Architectural designer Aziz Osko has updated the house, revisiting details from Neutra's original design that were never built.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Villa Sanlomjoy / Yangnar Studio
items.content_html: Rooted in childhood memories, the house began with a collection of salvaged wooden doors and windows, some sourced from Myanmar via Mae Sot, Tak, Thailand. Their character reflects an Anglo-Burmese synthesis, combining British Colonial proportions and European window typologies with traditional Burmese craftsmanship—wooden joinery, pegs, louvers, and casement windows. Rather than serving as decorative elements, these openings became the architectural framework of the house, defining its proportions, height, rhythm, and relationship with light and air.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Impermanence by Design: An Architectural History of Antarctica
items.content_html: "Antarctica is known through narratives," states Victoria Nuviala Antelo during the lecture on Inhabiting the Extreme: An Architectural Biography of Antarctica, presented at the Buenos Aires International Architecture Biennial. Indeed, throughout architectural history, numerous stories, experiences, ways of inhabiting, and building practices have often been excluded from official narratives. Buried beneath thick layers of ice, the history of Antarctic architecture tells a story of impermanence. The ice surrounding the continent expands and contracts each year, doubling its surface area, while the species that inhabit it migrate and return according to their life cycles. Ice covers structures as katabatic winds erase the traces of more than 200 years of human presence. Explorations, settlements, architectural interventions, and ways of inhabiting remain concealed within one of the most extreme landscapes on the planet.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Circular Town Hall Krimpenerwaard / Ector Hoogstad Architecten
items.content_html: Following the merger that established the municipality of Krimpenerwaard, the local government sought to unite its organization in one central town hall: a welcoming, accessible place for residents and entrepreneurs, a collaborative workplace, and an affordable building that would advance circular construction.

items.title: [ArchDaily] M38 House / Muda Prefab
items.content_html: The M38 House is born from a question: how can we industrialize construction without standardizing architecture? This 38 m² prefabricated house aligns domestic space design with manufacturing, transportation, and assembly processes. Its first unit is installed inside the workshop where it was built, serving as a showroom that allows visitors to experience the spaces and learn about the house's materials within its manufacturing context.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Cabin Budor / R21 Arkitekter
items.content_html: The commission consists of the design and construction of a weekend cabin in Budor. The main challenge is to integrate the volume into the landscape through its materiality, seeking to ensure that the project interferes as little as possible with the natural surroundings. The architecture aims to establish a dialogue with the landscape without attempting to dominate it.

items.title: [ArchDaily] “Architecture Must Return to Its Essence”: Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu on the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
items.content_html: "Architecture must return to its essence." With this statement, Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu establish the central premise of their curatorial vision for the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, taking place from May 8 to November 21, 2027, across the Giardini, the Arsenale, and throughout Venice. Titled "Do Architecture – For the Possibility of Coexistence Facing a Real Reality", the exhibition calls for a return to the physical act of making architecture, at a time when, according to the curators, the discipline has become increasingly disconnected from lived reality through excessive abstraction, commercialization, and digitalization.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Inherited Ground: Designing Houses on Contaminated Land
items.content_html: Industrial activity can end long before its effects disappear from the land. Factories close, buildings are demolished, and former industrial districts gradually become part of new residential developments. Yet the soil beneath them may still contain traces of their previous use, sometimes requiring extensive intervention before construction can begin.
